A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 31-page Mixture-of-Pathways paper, including Appendix A.1-A.9. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the material matches apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original computational experiments on 82 Mod-Cog tasks, including routing consistency, expert-removal tests, learning dynamics, ablations, and task accuracies in Tables 1-2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Mod-Cog experiments and their numerical and graphical outcomes, including the main results and supplementary analyses in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Algorithms 1-2 retain the same heterogeneous GRU experts, routing-cost objective, task-performance scaling, and expert-dropout procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 82 Mod-Cog cognitive tasks. Task descriptions, variants, and evaluated scenarios in Section 3.2 and Appendix A are unchanged.

E2.justification: The HMoE baseline and model variants retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. Tables 1-2 and the main and appendix figures add or remove no comparator.

E3.justification: Training budgets, input processing, model sizes, evaluation trials, pathway metrics, clustering procedures, and task-difficulty protocols are identical in the main text and appendices.

E4.justification: The dropout robustness sweep, complex-expert lesions, Table 1 ablations, effective-rank analysis, task-specific case studies, and alternative task-difficulty analysis are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report 20 runs for routing consistency, 10 runs for Table 1 ablations, and five GRU runs per task for difficulty estimation. Uncertainty displays and significance-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and graphical results match, including Table 2 mean accuracies of 91.1% for the baseline, 83.0% for the proposed model, and 90.1% without dropout. Appendix result entries and qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions and mathematical expressions for learned pathway complexity, losses, dropout probability, and effective rank are identical, including Equations 1-10 and Appendix A.3-A.5.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that heterogeneity alone is insufficient and that three inductive biases produce processing pathways with brain-like dynamics.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and neuroscience comparisons are unchanged. Section 6.1 retains the same limitations concerning backward routing, direct comparison with brain data, small-scale evaluation, and pathway measurement.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 retains identical implementation details, optimizer hyperparameters, and code-access information. Section 3.2 retains the same NVIDIA T4 hardware and approximately one-hour training-time disclosure.

R1.justification: Section 2, research-positioning statements elsewhere, and all 78 numbered reference entries are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 21 October 2025 to v3 dated 21 November 2025. Article wording, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 16 figures, two tables, algorithm displays, captions, and page arrangements remain identical. Rendered differences are confined to the updated first-page stamp text.

improvement.justification: v3 reproduces the methods, empirical evidence, mathematical content, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information of v2, including its appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date identification produces no meaningful gain or loss in paper quality.
